bug_description.normalized: The staged 5-byte witness drives the fuzz harness's selector byte `0xE6` through `Data[0] % platforms_len`, and with `CS_NEXT_VERSION == 5` that yields `27`, selecting the TMS320C64x backend. The remaining four bytes `89 62 63 99` are then consumed by the vulnerable instruction-word expression in `TMS320C64x_getInstruction()` and passed into `decodeInstruction_4()`. Because that source expression left-shifts `code[0]` without the cast added by the fix, this GT grounds the exact byte flow into the decoder rather than an exact source-level `insn` constant. The reproduced vulnerable run nevertheless reaches the print loop with a decoded `cs_insn` whose final public TMS320C64x instruction id is passed to `cs_insn_name()`. In vulnerable `TMS320C64xMapping.c`, `TMS320C64x_insn_name()` checks only `id < TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING` before indexing a 3-element `insn_name_maps` array by raw enum value. Because the enum is dense (`INVALID = 0, ABS = 1, ABS2 = 2, ADD = 3, ...`), any returned id >= 3 reads past that table. The stray pointer returned from this out-of-bounds read becomes the final `%s` argument to `fprintf()` in `fuzz_disasm.c`, and the saved MemorySanitizer trace records the ensuing READ/SEGV in `_IO_vfprintf`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that consumes the four attacker-controlled instruction bytes and builds the 32-bit expression handed to the TMS320C64x decoder; the decoded result later determines the public instruction id used as a name-table index.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 5-byte blob `e6 89 62 63 99`. After the harness selector byte chooses `CS_ARCH_TMS320C64X`, the remaining four bytes reach this statement as `code[0..3]`. Because the vulnerable expression left-shifts `code[0]` without the cast added by the fix, this trace grounds those exact bytes reaching the decoder input, not a source-level constant `insn` value.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable TMS320C64x instruction-name table contains only three contiguous array elements even though `TMS320C64x_insn_name()` later indexes it by raw dense enum value. The embedded `name_map.id` fields do not create sparse array slots, so only indices 0, 1, and 2 are in bounds. The fix replaces the truncated table with one entry per enum value.

sink.description: Project sink. The out-of-bounds pointer returned by `cs_insn_name(handle, i->id)` becomes the final `%s` argument to `fprintf()`, which immediately reaches the saved `_IO_vfprintf` crash.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant input is the exact four-byte decoder payload `89 62 63 99` as consumed by the instruction-word expression at line 599. On the reproduced path, decoding those bytes yields the public TMS320C64x instruction id later used to index `insn_name_maps`.

parser_admitted.description: The selector byte `0xE6` makes `i = Data[0] % 29 == 27`, so `cs_open()` installs the TMS320C64x big-endian backend and the remaining four bytes are admitted onto the crashing parser path.

fine_trace.code:
int i = (int)Data[0] % platforms_len;

err = cs_open(platforms[i].arch, platforms[i].mode, &handle);
fine_trace.note: The exact selector byte `0xE6` and `CS_NEXT_VERSION == 5` make `platforms_len == 29`, so `0xE6 % 29 == 27` and the harness selects `platforms[27] = { CS_ARCH_TMS320C64X, CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN }` before calling into the project disassembler.

The remaining witness bytes `89 62 63 99` are consumed here as the four-byte decoder input. Because `code[0]` is left-shifted without the cast added by the fix, this step grounds the exact bytes reaching the decoder expression rather than an exact source-level `insn` constant.

After one TMS320C64x instruction decodes successfully, `cs_disasm()` writes a public instruction id into the returned `cs_insn` with `handle->insn_id(...)` and then lets `fill_insn()` overwrite it with `MCInst_getOpcodePub(mci)` if the printer rewrites the mnemonic. Because the saved crash reaches the print loop at `fuzz_disasm.c:243`, this witness produced at least one `cs_insn`, and the surviving final `i->id` is the raw public TMS320C64x enum later passed to `cs_insn_name()`.

The vulnerable table has only three contiguous array elements even though `TMS320C64x_insn_name()` later uses a dense TMS320C64x enum as the array index. The stored `name_map.id` values do not create sparse slots, so only raw indices 0, 1, and 2 are in bounds even though the second and third elements mention `ADD` and `NOP`.

This is the only guard before the table lookup. It rejects ids outside the public enum range but never compares `id` against the 3-element extent of `insn_name_maps`; the later non-null bad `%s` pointer in the saved MSan crash shows the witness took the fall-through path `id < TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING`.

This line uses the final public instruction id as a raw array index. For the witness, the later non-null bad `%s` pointer in the saved MSan trace proves the final `id` was below `TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING` yet not one of the three in-bounds indices 0..2, so this read stepped past `insn_name_maps` and produced a stray `const char *`.

The out-of-bounds pointer returned in step 5 becomes the final `%s` argument to `fprintf()`. The saved MemorySanitizer run records `_IO_vfprintf` crashing on a READ from address `0x0000000a2e58`, with `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` at `fuzz_disasm.c:243:13` as the first project frame beneath libc.

crash_stack.function: fuzzer::FuzzerDriver(int*, char***, int (*)(unsigned char const*, unsigned long))

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Project sink `fprintf(..., cs_insn_name(handle, i->id))` at `suite/fuzz/fuzz_disasm.c:243` is the immediate caller beneath the saved libc/MSan frames, so the sink matches the observed crash path.

format.name: Capstone fuzz_disasmnext 5-byte witness
format.contract: The exact 5-byte binary blob `e6 89 62 63 99`. Byte 0 must be `0xE6` so `Data[0] % 29 == 27` selects `platforms[27] = { CS_ARCH_TMS320C64X, CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN }`. Bytes 1..4 are then the exact decoder-input bytes consumed by `TMS320C64x_getInstruction()` on the reproduced vulnerable path and ultimately yield a final public TMS320C64x id that `TMS320C64x_insn_name()` uses as a raw array index past the 3-element `insn_name_maps` table before the fuzzer prints the returned pointer with `%s`.
